We have template details. The retro_smarts_template shows transformation: product (left side) -> precursors (right side). The retro template: '[C:8]-[C@@H;D3;+0:9](-[C@H;D3;+0:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12])-[C@;H0;D4;+0:2](-[C:1])(-[OH;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7])>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7]).[C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]'

So retrosynthetic step: target molecule (product) is broken into two fragments: a carbonyl fragment (C1-C2(=O)-C4(F)3) and an alkene fragment (C8-CH= C... aromatic). The target molecule appears to be a bicyclic? Let's map.

Our target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We need to produce JSON route: root node is molecule (target). Children: one reaction node with template_id 1914384, children are precursor molecules (two). Need to get SMILES of precursors from applying template.

We can use apply_template tool.
